jobs.title: Youth Development Specialist, Alpha (Remote) - $120,000/year USD
jobs.description:
"All of my students came back in the top 1% for growth and achievement on their MAP scores."

— Sam DePalo, Lead Guide, Alpha Fort Worth Texas

Alpha is hiring.

Most youth development careers reward you for staying put. This one rewards you for arriving. You will land at a different Alpha campus every one to three months, walk in as a stranger to every student, parent and colleague, and have them working at full standard inside a week.

Alpha sends you where the network needs you, on site at campuses across the United States: one launching from nothing, or one running short-staffed. You do not choose the city. Accommodation is booked and paid for at every stop, and you earn a flat $120,000 wherever you live. You will be away from home every week outside of PTO.

Alpha is a private school where students finish core academics in two hours a day using adaptive software. The rest of the day goes to life skills: public speaking, focus, collaboration, and giving and taking feedback. You will not teach math or reading. You will run one-hour workshops where students build, debate and present, then coach them one to one against their own progress data until they hit their weekly targets.

Most people doing this work see one cohort in one city. You will see the whole network: which motivation strategies travel and which are local, and what separates a campus that is thriving from one that is struggling, because you will have worked in both inside the same year. You will also watch quiet students stand up and present to a room, in more than one state. Nothing prepares you faster to lead a campus of your own.

If the road is the point rather than the price, apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Run one-hour life skill workshops for K-8 students, adapting the provided curriculum to the cohort in front of you
Coach students one to one and in small groups using Coachbot analytics, weekly goals and incentives, until 90% or more hit their targets
Administer and score Test2Pass assessments so students prove the skill rather than just attend the session
Reach full standard inside your first week at each new campus, with names learned and rapport built
Hand over cleanly at the end of every posting, documenting per-student progress and every open intervention

What You Won’t Be Doing

Teaching core academic subjects, lecturing from the front of the room, or grading
Writing curriculum from scratch: workshop plans, analytics and playbooks are provided
Running campus operations, facilities or admissions
Filling in as a substitute with no authority and no accountability for student results
Funding your own travel: accommodation is booked and paid for at every posting

Youth Development Specialist Key Responsibilities

Hold student outcomes at full standard at whichever campus is launching or running short-staffed.

Basic Requirements

Based anywhere in the US, within reasonable reach of a major airport
Willing to be posted away from home one to three months at a time, with time at home only during PTO
Comfortable with Alpha assigning every posting, including the city and the campus
Bachelor's degree in any subject
At least 3 years working with K-8 students. Classroom experience is not required: camp counseling, coaching and youth program leadership all count
Able to describe one specific time you coached a K-8 student toward a goal, including the goal, what you did, and the result
Legal right to work in the US without visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

A track record of sustained mobility: travel-heavy field roles, touring programs, seasonal camp circuits, or service-year placements across multiple cities
Experience running youth workshops in camps, athletics, enrichment programs or youth leadership settings
Comfort reading student progress dashboards or learning analytics to decide where to intervene
Experience coaching a disengaged student to a measurable improvement you can point to

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

This is a full-time, W2 employee position with immediate access to benefits (https://support.crossover.com/article/7581-w2-benefits-u-s-paychex-paid-only). All roles are year-long positions. The compensation level for this role is $120,000 USD/year. The payment period is weekly. Consult www.crossover.com/help-and-faqs for more details on this topic.

jobs.description:
About Our Job

With competitive pay, great benefits, and endless opportunities, working for the City and County of Denver means seeing yourself working with purpose — for you, and those who benefit from your passion, skills and expertise. Join our diverse, inclusive and talented workforce of more than 11,000 team members who are at the heart of what makes Denver, Denver.

What We Offer

The City and County of Denver offers competitive pay commensurate with education and experience. New hires are typically brought into the organization between $74,276 and $98,415 based on experience and education. We also offer generous benefits for full-time employees which include but are not limited to:

A guaranteed life-long monthly pension, once vested after 5 years of service
457B Retirement Plan
140 hours of PTO earned within first year + 12 paid holidays, 1 personal holiday, 1 Wellness Day and 1 volunteer day per year
Competitive medical, dental and vision plans effective within 1 month of start date

Location & Schedule

The City and County of Denver supports a hybrid workplace model. Employees work where needed, at a job site several days a week and off-site as needed. Employees must work within the state of Colorado on their off-site days. In this position you can expect to work on site at the Wellington E. Webb Municipal Building, 201 W. Colfax Ave., Denver, CO 80202 or in other community locations Mondays through Wednesdays. There may be other additional in-person requirements on some Thursdays and Fridays. There may also be occasional evening or weekend hours to meet the needs of community partners as well as local travel to partner sites and youth programs across Denver as needed. This position will be fast paced with frequent interruptions and changing priorities

Who We Are & What You’ll Do

The Office of Children's Affairs (OCA) is seeking an OST Program Manager to lead the City's work to ensure high-quality out-of-school time experiences for young people across Denver. This position leads OCA's OST program, including the Denver Afterschool Alliance (DAA). It sets program goals and quality standards, manages the program budget and contracted partners, and builds the skills of the adults and systems that support youth. The role helps create equitable, developmentally appropriate environments across Denver's OST ecosystem.

Specifically, as the OST Program Manager of OCA you will:

Program Leadership and Strategy (approx. 25%)

Set goals, policies, and quality standards for OCA's OST program, and revise processes as the program grows
Design new services or change existing ones to strengthen program quality and reach
Gather input from youth, families, and partners to shape OCA's OST strategy and policy direction
Develop solutions to complex issues that cross agencies or systems and affect the program's future

Denver Afterschool Alliance and Partner Management (approx. 25%)

Serve as OCA's primary point of contact for DAA member organizations
Convene and support the DAA leadership team
Plan and lead citywide OST convenings, communities of practice, and learning events
Hold regular check-ins with all contracted partners, and plan and oversee the work of partners, vendors, and consultants in the program

Quality, Training, and Coaching (approx. 25%)

Lead site visits and observational assessments to make sure programs meet quality standards and best practices
Coach partners with clear, actionable feedback, including youth-serving organizations and employer partners
Design and oversee evidence-based training for OST staff and youth-serving organizations on topics such as positive youth development, trauma-informed practice, and social and emotional learning (SEL)

Budget, Contracts, and Evaluation (approx. 15%)

Develop and manage the OST program budget, prepare budget reports, and make resource allocation recommendations
Partner with OCA’s Contract Administrator to oversee grant and contract administration for the program area
Manage program evaluation, using training data, site assessments, and partner feedback to measure results and guide citywide quality improvement
Prepare reports, including an annual report on program results

Stakeholder Engagement and Representation (approx. 10%)

Act as spokesperson for OCA's OST program with internal and external groups
In collaboration with the YDE Administrator, build strong relationships with community organizations, schools, and city agencies such as Denver Economic Development & Opportunity (DEDO), Denver Public Schools (DPS), and Denver Parks & Recreation
Represent OCA in coalitions focused on OST, youth development, and youth employment, and contribute to policy and program design that centers youth voice and equity
Keep leadership informed of legislative and policy changes affecting OST
Other related duties as assigned

What You’ll Bring

We value diversity of ethnicity, race, socioeconomic status, sexual identity, gender, religion, language, ability, and experience and exemplify this through the makeup of our team at all levels. You'll be right at home here if you cultivate strong relationships and push yourself, your work, the people around you and Denver to the next level.

Our ideal candidate has some or all the following experience, skills, and characteristics:

Leadership experience in out-of-school time, including coordinating programs across multiple sites, partners, or funding streams in a nonprofit, school district, government, or intermediary setting
Track record of facilitating multi-stakeholder coalitions, advisory groups, or communities of practice, and planning convenings or learning events
Experience managing contracted partners, vendors, or consultants toward shared outcomes
Knowledge of Denver's youth-serving landscape and established relationships with community organizations, schools, and city agencies
Familiarity with recognized OST quality frameworks and tools, such as the Weikart Center Youth Program Quality Assessment (YPQA)
Demonstrated ability to design and deliver training for adult learners and to coach staff using observation-based, actionable feedback
Strong understanding of positive youth development, adolescent development, trauma-informed practice, SEL, and equity-centered practice
Experience managing program budgets and grants, including public or braided funding sources
Experience using data and evaluation to measure program results and guide quality improvement
Bilingual in English and Spanish

Required Minimum Qualifications

Education requirement: Bachelor's Degree in Public Administration, Management, Sociology, Psychology, Political Science, or a related field
Experience Requirement: Three (3) years of full performance professional level experience developing, implementing, and administering programs
Education/Experience Equivalency: One (1) year of the appropriate type and level of experience may be substituted for each required year of post high school education for all classifications. Additional appropriate education may be substituted for the minimum experience requirements
Licensure: None

Application Deadline

This position is expected to stay open until October 14th, 2026. Please submit your application as soon as possible and no later than October 14th, 2026 at 11:59 PM MSTat 11:59 PM MST

Brief Description

Family Services Case Manager (SR0093)

About The Role

Maximum Term Contract / Part time (0.8 FTE)
Salary packaging, gifted leave at Christmas and Easter
Competitive above-award salary, SCHADS Level 5.1 - $102,791.52 pro rata

Maximum Term Contract until 31 March 2027.

Role Purpose

Working within the Bayside Peninsula Integrated Family Services team, you will play a key role in promoting the safety, stability and development of children, young people and their families. You will deliver evidence-based interventions through a tailored, family-centred case management approach, responding to risk and vulnerability with a whole-of-family focus.

In this role, you will work collaboratively with families to support children and young people up to 18 years of age who may be experiencing complex and interconnected challenges, including trauma, school refusal, family violence and involvement with multiple service systems (such as NDIS). This is a diverse and fast-paced role, requiring sound judgement, responsiveness and the ability to act decisively to address risk.

In this contracted role until 31st March 2027
, you will work alongside a caring and collaborative team, based in the Good Shepherd Hastings office, with frequent outreach and engagement across the peninsula.

Key Responsibilities

Strengthen parenting capacity, confidence and skills to support positive outcomes for children and young people
Enhance the wellbeing of children, young people and their families through culturally responsive, client-centred practice
Prevent child abuse and neglect through early intervention and timely, targeted support
Support families through significant life transitions and periods of crisis, maintaining a focus on safety and stability
Work collaboratively within a multi-disciplinary and multi-system environment, including participation in care team, school and stakeholder meetings

About You

Tertiary qualification in Social Work, Psychology, or related discipline such as nursing, early childhood or child protection
Experience in child protection, child and family services, or working within a best interests framework
Sound understanding of systems theory and trauma-informed practice
A persistent and strengths-based practitioner who actively advocates for children, young people and families
Ability to work collaboratively as part of a care team and broader service network to deliver wrap-around support
Experience working with The Orange Door is highly regarded

Benefits

Salary packaging - up to $15,900 in tax-free pay per year, plus entertainment up to $2650
4 days gifted leave at Christmas and Easter (pro rata)
Additional leave through purchase leave pathways
Employee Assistance Program, a free and confidential counselling service
Eligible for participation in the portable long service leave program

Our 2023-2027 strategy outlines the world we want to see and our role in advancing it. We aspire for all women, girls, and families to be safe, well, strong, and connected. We strive for equity, dignity and social justice for women, girls and families by collaborating globally and acting locally, supporting our communities in Australia and New Zealand to thrive.

We want women, girls and families to live full and dignified lives, have dignified income and enjoy financial wellbeing. We aim to provide place-based, people-centred, holistic services while working at the system level to achieve bold and audacious reform. We currently offer microfinance programs and products, financial counselling and coaching, family and domestic violence support services, family and youth programs, playgroups, education programs and community houses. These services are complemented by research and strong advocacy to address the underlying structural causes of injustice, exclusion, and inequality.

General Description

The purpose of the Health Education Division is to address community health priorities by influencing decisions and actions that individuals, groups and communities make with the goals of preventing disease and disability and improving health outcomes. The Division strives to help individuals and communities improve their health at the micro and macro level, by increasing knowledge and influencing attitudes related to health; advancing policies and systems that support healthy choices; and effecting social determinants of health, including adverse childhood experiences and exposure to violence.

This position will work with community partners working to support family and community resilience in the Durham community. The position will be part of a team working to identify strengths and barriers to health and wellbeing for families and coordinate solutions across partners. This position will ensure timely distribution of information about community resources and programs. This position will work alongside the Adverse Childhood Experiences and Resilience Coordinator to facilitate education events for community members, service and healthcare providers, and community partners related to family and community resilience.

The functions listed below are those that represent the majority of the time spent working in this position. Management may assign additional functions related to the type of work of the position as necessary.

Participate as a member of the Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs) and Resilience team; assist with collaboration with community partners to achieve shared goals.
Gather, arrange, and distribute information about community events, resources, and programs among service and healthcare providers.
Work with community partners to identify system and community-level barriers and community strengths to family and community resilience.
Collaborate with community members and partners to facilitate educational events on topics related to resilience, trauma-informed care, and mental wellbeing.

Also involves exerting between 20 and 50 pounds of force on a regular and recurring basis or skill, adeptness and speed in the use of the fingers, hands or limbs on repetitive operation of mechanical or electronic office or shop machines or tools within moderate tolerances or limits of accuracy.

Empathy

"We are never going to lower the standard for any kid — instead we're going to raise the support to help them get there."

— Braden, Head Guide, Alpha Austin

Alpha is hiring.

The most supportive thing you can do for a student who hits 99% of their weekly goal is refuse to call it done. Not because you are indifferent, but because you believe they can clear the bar, and lowering it is the real failure.

You are not running a classroom. At Alpha, students learn academics through AI-powered adaptive learning apps. No lectures. No textbooks. No whiteboard. Motivation and life skills, the parts of youth work that usually happen around the edges of a program, are the whole job here.

Picture a Tuesday. Half your day you run one-hour workshops for a K-8 cohort on public speaking, focus, and how to give and receive real feedback. The other half you sit with those same students one-on-one or in small groups, read their Coachbot analytics, and push each of them to 100% of their weekly app goals, using school currency, leaderboards, and the relationship you have built with them to break through resistance.

Your quarter comes down to three numbers: every student in your cohort hits their weekly app goals, every student passes the Test2Pass mastery check for each workshop, and 90% or more say they love you. Missing one of the three is missing the job.

The payoff is the day a student who spent September insisting they were bad at math asks you to raise their goal.

This is a full-time, on-site role at one of Alpha's campuses. We recruit nationally, so job boards may display this opportunity in nearby cities that do not have a campus yet.

Current openings for this salary tier are available in Scottsdale, AZ; Los Angeles, CA; Miami, FL; Oklahoma City and Tulsa, OK; Nashville, TN; and Austin, Dallas, and Plano, TX.

If you're interested in another Alpha campus, apply anyway and tell us your preferred location—we'll consider you for the appropriate opening.

If you have coached youth sports, run a cabin at camp, or worked with a kid who wanted to quit, the last step before an offer is a full day on campus coaching real Alpha students. If that day is the part you want most, apply today

What You Will Be Doing

Leading one-hour life-skills workshops for K-8 cohorts on public speaking, focus, and giving and receiving feedback
Running daily 1:1 and small-group motivation sessions that push every student to 100% of their weekly app goals, using Coachbot analytics and Alpha's incentive systems (school currency, leaderboards)
Administering the Test2Pass mastery assessment for each life skill, then re-coaching any student who does not pass until they do
Adapting the workshop playbook, and building new sessions when you find a gap, so the same material lands with a kindergartener and with an 8th grader
Being both the adult who holds the standard and the adult your students choose to talk to

What You Won’t Be Doing

Lecturing at a whiteboard, writing math and reading lesson plans, or grading homework; academic instruction lives in the apps

Supervising kids at computers; motivation here is active and personal

Youth Counselor Key Responsibilities

Ensure every student in your K-8 cohort hits their weekly learning goals, masters each life skill, and leaves the year saying they loved school.

Basic Requirements

Willing to work in person at an Alpha campus in Scottsdale, AZ; Los Angeles, CA; Miami, FL; Oklahoma City or Tulsa, OK; Nashville, TN; or Austin, Dallas, or Plano, TX - relocation support provided
Bachelor's degree in any subject
At least 3 years working directly with K-8 (elementary and middle school) students: classroom teaching, tutoring, athletic coaching, camp leadership, or youth program work
Comfortable letting adaptive learning software deliver the academic instruction while you own motivation and life-skills coaching
A personal record of high achievement, academic, athletic, or professional, that made holding a hard standard a habit rather than a posture
Stage presence strong enough to hold a room of 12-year-olds for an hour without raising your voice
Legal right to work in the United States without visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Youth athletics coaching, debate, drama, camp leadership, or after-school program work where you were personally accountable for kids hitting a specific goal
Experience teaching social-emotional learning (SEL) or durable-skills curricula

Daily use of generative AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

x5 roles

Full time, 35 hours per week. You will need to be available to work over the Christmas period and on Bank Holidays from 21 December 2026 to 12 January 2027, with time of in lieu given in accordance with Crisis’ TOIL policy.

Fixed term contract until 31 March 2027

About The Role

This is an exciting time to join the Christmas Case Management Team at Crisis. This Christmas we’re determined to make our biggest impact yet and so we’re investing in the team who work across the Crisis at Christmas services in London and through an outreach-based approach thereafter. We are therefore looking to recruit five brand new case managers to support even more of our guests this year.

The role of a case manager within the Christmas Case Management Team is a varied and fulfilling role. Through collaboration with internal and external partners and advocating where necessary, you will support guests to achieve their outcomes and move away from homelessness. You will record and monitor the progress of service users, ensuring the data is accurate. You will receive regular supervision, reflective practice, and access to learning and development opportunities. Finally, you will be joining a highly experienced, motivated and supportive team seeking to improve the quality of life of people experiencing homelessness in London. 

About You

We are looking for an experienced, skilled and driven people to join the team as Case Managers. Working in a fast-paced environment, you will establish open and trusting relationships with people who are/have been living on the streets or in temporary accommodation, offering high-quality information, advice and support and working in a psychologically informed way. 

Many of our guests are distressed by their situation and, and the role would suit people who are both compassionate and resilient. You’ll be able to draw on your experience of coaching and providing information, advice and guidance to provide flexible, person-centred support to people who are homeless, assisting them to access accommodation and relevant services. It’s vital therefore that you have a solid knowledge and understanding of the issues affecting people experiencing homelessness including a good understanding of homelessness legislation and benefits entitlement.

Our staff, members and volunteers are vital to getting the right government policies in place, providing breakthrough services, and building a supportive community. We’ll lead by example to nurture a positive and ambitious workplace guided by ending homelessness.

As a member of the team, you will have access to a wide range of employee benefits including:

A competitive salary. Please note our salaries are fixed to counter inequity and we do not negotiate at offer stage.
Interest free loans for travel season ticket, cycle to work, and deposit to secure a tenancy.
Pension scheme with an employer contribution of 8.5%
28 days’ annual leave (pro rata) which increases with service to 31 days and the option to purchase up to 10 additional days leave.
Enhanced maternity, paternity, shared parental, and adoption pay.
Wellbeing Leave to be used flexibly
And more! (Full list of benefits available on website)

Alongside our excellent staff benefits, we will support your ongoing development to build your skills, experience, and career.

When you join us, you will have the opportunity to join our staff diversity networks, which aim to champion issues across the organisation, enable staff to be their authentic and best selves and contribute to making Crisis a truly diverse organisation.
